is_anopheles.evidence: A total of 1,405 anopheline mosquitoes were collected from 21 localities throughout Cameroon and identified as An. gambiae (N = 1,248; 88.8%), An. arabiensis (N = 120; 8.5%) and An. melas (N = 37; 2.6%). (Page 1, Abstract)

reports_target_markers.evidence: Two mutations at position 1014... known as kdr (knockdown resistance) mutations leading to a change of a Leucine to a Phenylalanine (L1014F) or to a Serine (L1014S) confer resistance to DDT and pyrethroid insecticides in the insect. (Page 1, Abstract)

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 (Page 5) provides the number of mosquitoes (N) and the allelic frequencies (%) for 1014L, 1014F, and 1014S across 21 localities. Page 4 also states that all An. arabiensis and An. melas were homozygous susceptible.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were sampled in 21 locations (Table 1) spanning the whole of Cameroon... (Page 2, Study sites)

is_primary_study.evidence: The current report provides a detailed update of the occurrence, frequency and geographic distribution of both L1014F and L1014S kdr mutations within and among An. gambiae populations from throughout Cameroon. (Page 2)

sub_country_location.evidence: Table 1 (Page 3) lists 21 localities (e.g., Ngousso, Nkolondom, Dabadi) with their geographic coordinates.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected between May 2005 and May 2007... (Page 2, Mosquito collections)

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the authors have published previous studies on resistance in Cameroon (e.g., Etang et al. 2006, Nwane et al. 2009), this paper presents a comprehensive update and new collection data from 2005-2007.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype frequency and sample size data are provided in Table 2 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study provides a detailed distribution map and frequency analysis of the Vgsc L1014F and L1014S kdr mutations in Anopheles gambiae s.s. (M and S molecular forms), An. arabiensis, and An. melas across 21 localities in Cameroon. Samples were collected between 2005 and 2007. Both kdr alleles were identified in both molecular forms of An. gambiae s.s., with higher frequencies in the S-form (An. gambiae) than the M-form (An. coluzzii). An. arabiensis and An. melas were found to be homozygous susceptible at the 1014 locus.
